source.title: Implicit Regularization with Polynomial Growth in Deep Tensor Factorization
source.authors: Kais Hariz; Hachem Kadri; S. Ayache; Maher Moakher; T. Artières

record.tranche_reason: Reports original experiments on depth and generalization in overparameterized tensor completion, a setting outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies deep tensor factorization for tensor completion, not classification of natural versus random labels. Its experiments report generalization and validation losses as depth and missing-data percentage vary. It does not test any listed version directly.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes depth-dependent implicit regularization in CP tensor completion. None of its results tests V1–V8: depth is varied rather than width, and tensor reconstruction loss and effective rank do not measure the behaviors or comparisons those versions name. Citing Neyshabur et al. does not make this a test of V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion. They derive depth-dependent polynomial block-norm dynamics under balanced-initialization assumptions and argue that these promote greedy low-rank recovery. Their experiments suggest that deeper factorizations attain low-rank and low-generalization-loss solutions more consistently across initializations. This is a robustness claim, not a claim that the best validation loss decreases monotonically with depth.
record.recipe_differences: Overparameterized deep CP tensor factorization optimized by gradient descent for tensor completion; not the listed classifier experiments or their recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, initialization, and percentage of observed tensor entries change the reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports the best validation loss across initializations for each depth and missing-entry percentage. These minima do not improve monotonically with depth: depth 3 is best at 75% missing entries, whereas depth 0 is best at 85% and 90%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In overparameterized CP tensor completion, the best validation loss found across initializations depends jointly on factorization depth and data coverage; greater depth does not uniformly improve that minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 5.2–5.4 and Figures 4–5 report that deeper synthetic tensor factorizations more consistently attain low effective rank and low generalization loss across initializations. Low loss remains attainable at any tested depth. These distributions are not recorded by the selected minima in R1–R18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing CP factorization depth can make low-rank recovery and low reconstruction error more robust to initialization in tensor completion.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.5 and Appendix B report similar depth-related rank behavior on Meteo-UK and CCDS data, including a Meteo-UK experiment using rank-one matrix initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-related implicit bias toward lower effective rank also occurs in the tested real-world tensor-completion settings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: Experiments use tensor completion and synthetic data for the main analysis; results are sensitive to initialization. Several plotted findings are not numerically tabulated, and 11 of 1500 runs that diverged or yielded rank zero were excluded from Figure 4.

untested.parts: Paired random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classification and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as a correlate of generalization gaps and its ranking against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 values and missing-entry conditions are transcribed correctly. The table's selected minima cannot establish robustness across initializations; that conclusion rests on Figures 4–5 and their accompanying text. Figure 4 excludes 11 of 1500 runs that diverged or yielded rank zero. No omitted result bears on V1–V8, so missing is empty.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy in the listed image classifiers.
Width sweeps of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
